newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle closes mixed, feeders higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle closes mixed, feeders higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed, underpinned by talk that packers could be poised to raise their bids in the cash market shortly, while feeders ended higher despite surging CBOT corn prices.
Dealers said the performance of feeders was "phenomenal" in view of the strength of CBOT corn. Concern about a shortage of feeder cattle later in the year has contributed to the market's strength.
August feeders closed 0.325 cent a lb higher at 80.825 cents despite the key new-crop December CBOT corn contract closing 7-1/2 cents a bushel higher at $2.56-1/2.
Dealers said buyers in August were scattered while Cargill Investor Services was a featured buyer of November and January in what was seen as possibly fund-related activity.

August feeders set a contract high of 82.00 cents on Friday, the highest level for the nearby month since March 1994. The CME feeder index recently peaked at $81.72 per cwt, as of July 10, its highest level since April 12, 1994.
"Cash (feeder cattle) is very strong," one dealer said.
The latest CME feeder index, as of July 14, was up $0.37 at $81.44.
The cash live cattle market remained quiet with packers still bidding $62, steady with trade late last week, while offers remained in the $64 to $65 range.
There was talk, however, that packers may soon raise their bid to at least $63, possibly late Wednesday.
Dealers said packers would be keen to get some cover ahead of Friday's key U.S. Department of Agriculture cattle-on-feed and cattle inventory reports.
Featured buyers of August live cattle included E.D. and F. Man International, LIT, Dean Witter and Cargill Investor Services. Selling interest was scattered, dealers said.
LIT was also a featured buyer of October live cattle, while late selling of October from Cargill Investor Services, Refco and Lind Waldock prompted a weak finish, they added.
August closed 0.425 cent higher at 65.850 cents with other months 0.425 cent lower to 0.525 cent up.
